questions.prompt: A speed loop asks for more than the motor can deliver for a while and the integrator keeps accumulating. What happens when the setpoint becomes reachable again?
options: The integrator resets itself and nothing special happens.
The proportional term cancels the stored integral at once.
The stored integral keeps the output saturated, so the speed overshoots or recovers late (windup).
The encoder count wraps around and the loop faults.
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup
questions.explanation: Without anti-windup the integral keeps growing while the output is clipped, and it must be unwound by negative error before the output leaves saturation.

questions.prompt: 1440 counts per output revolution, a 10 ms tick, 17 counts counted in one tick. Speed in rad/s, precision 0.01.
Same encoder (1440 counts per revolution) read at 1 kHz. What is the smallest nonzero speed in rad/s, precision 0.01?
questions.explanation: 2*pi / (1440 * 0.001) = 4.363 rad/s, ten times coarser than at 100 Hz.

questions.prompt: A step test gives plant gain K = 10 rad/s per unit of u and a time constant of 0.2 s. For lambda tuning with tau_c = 0.1 s (Kp = tau/(K tau_c)), what is Kp, precision 0.001?
Why should the speed loop run from a timer tick rather than from a loop that ends with delay(10)?
options: The real period would include the work time and any blocking calls, so dt in the integral and speed formulas would be wrong.
delay() cannot be used with analogWrite.
A timer tick makes the PWM frequency higher.
questions.explanation: The formulas assume exactly dt between updates. Work time, Serial prints and jitter make the real period differ, scaling both the speed estimate and the integral gain.

questions.prompt: Dead zone 40 of 255. Controller output u = 0.6. Signed duty (round to an integer; the answer is positive).
Name four safety gates a motor-speed firmware should have and what each does to the output.
rubric: Command timeout or watchdog: forces zero output when no valid command arrives within a few command periods.
Output clamp (and optionally a ramp): limits u and how fast it may change.
Stall detection and current limit: high duty with almost no speed, or too much current, zeroes the output and latches a fault.
Safe boot state and integrator reset: outputs zero at start and when the loop is disabled.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
